methods.name: TAKE THE LIMIT
methods.outcome: Defined the D-scale pressure and critical reference radius; proved a coefficient-root/abscissa sufficient criterion for scalar degree noise.

methods.name: ASK WHO ELSE HAS THIS SHAPE
methods.outcome: Combined the exact symmetrized-code orbit collision formula with weighted Cauchy and the classical MacWilliams identity to prove 1+chi2 >= 4^{-k}(1+q)^E for every coordinate-permutation symmetrization.

methods.name: ADD THE POINTS AT INFINITY
methods.outcome: Applied the MacWilliams collision lower bound to Mao's alternating-form construction and proved D-scale pressure diverges for every fixed q>0, so q_c=0; identified the obstruction at ambient degree j/D -> infinity rather than degree reassembly.

new_results: For a binary linear code C <= F_2^E of dimension k and any finite coordinate-permutation group G, the symmetrized noised law satisfies 1+chi2(T_sqrt(q) P_{C,G} || U_E) >= 4^{-k}(1+q)^E for 0<=q<=1.
If k_n/E_n -> R and E_n/D_n -> infinity, then every q with log(1+q)>2R log 2 has infinite D-scale pressure; in the low-rate case R=0 the critical reference radius is q_c=0.

Mao's construction is uniform on the image of a linear map from Alt(K) before vertex relabeling, with k_n <= binom(K,2)=O((log n)^{2r}), E_n=binom(n,2), and D_n=Theta((log n)^{r-1}); hence its D-scale noised chi-square pressure tends to +infinity at every fixed q>0.
For arbitrary scalar degree spectra, Gamma=limsup_n sup_{j>D_n} b_{n,j}^{1/j}; if q Gamma<1 then the noised high-degree tail vanishes geometrically.
